questions.question: What condition on the Lorentz-breaking background vector follows when it is embedded in a chiral superfield?

options.A: ξμ=∂μS, with S a complex scalar
options.B: ξμ is an unconstrained constant vector
options.C: ξμ must equal the gauge field Aμ
options.D: ξμ is the derivative of the vector superfield's fermion

questions.rationale: The chiral proposal identifies the background vector with the gradient of its scalar component.

questions.question: What restriction on the CPT-even K tensor does the chiral-background route introduce?

options.A: Its tensor structure is fixed by a complex scalar field through ∂S and ∂S*
options.B: It retains the most general independent Riemann-symmetric components
options.C: It requires a vector superfield to hold ξμ

questions.rationale: The authors state the chiral multiplet fixes a special K form from a complex scalar.
questions.evidence_quote: completely ﬁxed by a complex scalar ﬁeld

questions.question: Which superfield is needed to reproduce the specific ansatz with ˜κμν=κ(ξμξν−ημνξ²/4)?

options.C: A tensor superfield of spin two

questions.rationale: For the restricted vector-background ansatz, the paper uses a vector superfield.
questions.evidence_quote: a vector superﬁeld must be used to accommodate the background vector

questions.question: What is a key difference in background component content between the chiral and vector constructions?

options.A: The vector-superfield case has a richer set of partners
options.B: The chiral case includes no scalar component
options.C: The vector case eliminates all fermionic components
options.D: The chiral case necessarily includes a spin-two partner

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly contrast the richer partner content of the vector option.
questions.evidence_quote: The content of partners is richer in this case than in the case of the chiral background.

questions.question: In the chiral construction, which component determines Kμνκλ, and which potential contributions are absent?

options.A: Only the scalar S gradient; neither ζ condensate nor G enters K
options.B: Only the fermion ζ and auxiliary G; S cancels
options.C: The gauge field Aμ alone; all background fields vanish
options.D: The auxiliary D and vector ξμ; the scalar is irrelevant

questions.rationale: The paper says K depends exclusively on S's gradient and has no ζ or G dependence.
questions.evidence_quote: K-tensor depends exclusively on the gradient of S.

questions.question: What symmetry properties characterize the CPT-even Kμνκλ tensor in the bosonic model?

options.A: Antisymmetry within each index pair, pair exchange symmetry, and vanishing double trace
options.B: Symmetry in every index and nonzero double trace
options.D: No index symmetries, but a vanishing single trace

questions.rationale: Equation (2) lists the Riemann-like pair symmetries and double-traceless condition.

questions.question: What happens to the ξμξνFμκFκν term when it is supersymmetrized in the vector-background construction?

options.A: A ξ²F² term appears automatically in the combination
options.B: It can be generated only by adding a matter multiplet

questions.rationale: The authors state the ξ²F² companion comes out automatically.

questions.question: What is the stated auxiliary-field consequence of Lorentz breaking in the chiral setup when ζ=G=0 and ∂μS≠0?

options.A: D is fixed nontrivially by the gauge-field strength even without matter coupling
options.B: D vanishes identically unless charged matter is present
options.C: D becomes an independent constant unrelated to Fμν
options.D: D acquires a mass from the photino condensate

questions.rationale: Under those background conditions, the displayed solution makes D depend on Fμν.
questions.evidence_quote: the breaking of Lorentz-symmetry, ﬁxes the auxiliary ﬁeld to be non-trivial

questions.question: What does the paper say can be inferred about the relative timing of SUSY and Lorentz-symmetry breaking?

options.A: The background signals SUSY violation, but the authors cannot determine which breaking occurred first
options.B: Lorentz breaking must always precede SUSY breaking
options.C: SUSY breaking is proven to occur only after Lorentz breaking
options.D: The two symmetries remain exact for either background

questions.rationale: They explicitly state they lack elements to decide whether SUSY breaking preceded Lorentz breaking.
questions.evidence_quote: we do not have elements to decide

questions.question: Why do the authors warn that nonphysical excitations remain an open issue?

options.A: Restrictions on the background may be needed to avoid tachyons and ghosts in the spectrum
options.B: The component action contains no fermions to cancel anomalies
options.C: The K tensor necessarily violates CPT
options.D: The vector-superfield proposal has no Lorentz-breaking vacuum

questions.rationale: They identify the spectrum and avoidance of tachyons/ghosts as an important question for future work.
